2  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.
The claimants, being aggrieved by the exoneration of liability on the insurer and also the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal for the death of their son - Raghavendra, are in appeal.
2. The facts of the case are that the accident occurred on 25.02.2016 between a lorry and a Swift D.zire car, in which the deceased was traveling.

3. The averments in the claim petition was that the lorry abruptly reduced the speed and as a result of which, the accident occurred and which has resulted in the death of Raghavendra, one of the inmates of the car.

4. The Tribunal by placing reliance on the charge sheet that had been laid against the driver of the car has come to the conclusion that the accident occurred only due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the car and has made the owner of the car liable for compensation and has proceeded to exonerate NC: 2024:KHC:51066 the driver of the lorry and thereafter, also exonerated the insurer of the lorry from the liability to pay compensation.
5.

Learned counsel for the insurer places reliance on the judgment of the Apex Court in Civil Appeal No.10145/2016 to contend that in similar circumstances, the Apex Court has held that the driver of the car who was following a truck would be responsible for the accident and the Tribunal was therefore justified in exonerating the driver of the lorry.
6.
In my view, this argument cannot be accepted.

In the case before the Apex Court, the driver of the car had been examined as PW.2 and he had admitted that at the time of the accident, the distance between the truck and the Maruthi car was only 10 to 15 feet.
In the instant case, there was no such evidence.
The owner of the lorry was placed exparte.
The assertion of the claimant that the lorry abruptly NC: 2024:KHC:51066 reduced the speed which caused the accident was not denied.
The insurer has not examined the driver of the lorry to establish that the car was in fact driven very close to the lorry.

Merely because a charge sheet has been laid against the driver of the car that would not take away the pleadings of the claimant that the lorry driver abruptly reduced the speed, which had caused the accident.
7. In such cases, the best witness to talk about the accident would be the driver of the lorry as well as the driver of the car.

When both the drivers were not examined by the respective parties, it cannot be assumed that the car which was traveling behind the lorry and came in contact with the lorry at the rear end was responsible for the accident.
8. If as a matter of fact, the lorry has abruptly reduced the speed, in my view, it would also have contributed to the accident though not full at least in part.
The driver of the lorry is therefore held responsible for NC: 2024:KHC:51066 the accident to the extent of 50% and consequently, the insurer of the lorry would also be liable to that extent.

sentences.text: As far as compensation is concerned, the deceased was aged 22 years and was unmarried.
The Tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.8,000/- since there was no proof of actual income.
In such circumstances, it would be appropriate to adopt the notional income determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which, for the accident of the year 2016, would be Rs.9,500/-.

Since the deceased was 22 years, 40% requires to be added as future prospects and since he was a bachelor, 50% requires to be deducted towards personal expenses, which makes his income to be Rs.6,650/- (Rs.9,500 + 40% = Rs.13,300 - 50% = Rs.6,650).
Consequently, the claimants would be entitled to Rs.14,36,400/- (Rs.6,650/- X 12 X 18) towards loss of dependency.
The claimants being parents, each of them would be entitled to a sum of Rs.48,400/- i.e., in all Rs.96,800/- towards loss of consortium.
They would also be entitled to Rs.36,300/- under conventional heads.
11. Thus, the claimants would be entitled to Rs.15,69,500/- as against Rs.9,09,000/- as compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
12. The insurer of the lorry would also be liable to pay 50% of the aforesaid compensation.
13. The other aspects of the award of the Tribunal shall remain undisturbed.
14. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
